rationale: Section 7(a) does contain a nominally mutual cap and 7(b) has a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, but the clause fails the fallback on carve-outs and on cap basis. The only stated exception is "CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9", and Paragraph 9 is the Independent Contractor clause — so the exception is an inoperative cross-reference and there is no carve-out for confidentiality (§ 8), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement (the § 5(c) non-infringement warranty) or indemnification (the document contains no indemnity clause at all despite the § 7 heading). The fallback requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; none survive here. The basis is also narrower than 12 months' fees: Contractor's cap is limited to fees actually paid for the particular Services under the relevant Statement of Work, which for a short or partly-invoiced SOW can fall below six months' fees. We therefore moved to the preferred position — mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with the standard Excluded Claims sentence uncapped, and confirming Clear Capital's fee payment obligations are not capped damages.

rationale: The pricing terms sit in § 3 (Contractor's Compensation), which provides only for time-and-materials compensation per Statement of Work, expense reimbursement, invoicing detail, rate-change notice and taxes. Searches across the full agreement for MFN-style language ("most favoured/favored nation", "no less favorable", "favorable", "best price/pricing/terms/rates", "other customers") returned no hits, and no other section contains a pricing or benchmarking covenant. There is therefore no obligation requiring Clear Capital to extend RadialSpark terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers, which meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer). Nothing to redline. Noted for information only (not a deviation under this rule): § 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap — a pricing point addressed under the price-increase rule rather than here.

quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment on Clear Capital. Services are engaged "on a task by task basis" under individually negotiated Statements of Work (p0004), and compensation is strictly time and materials as set out in each SOW plus actual out-of-pocket expenses (p0013), i.e. fees are payable only for services actually ordered and performed. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take-or-pay", "guarantee", "volume" and "quota" returned no take-or-pay, minimum-fee, guaranteed-hours or usage-cap provisions, and § 6 permits termination for convenience on fifteen days' notice whenever no SOW is outstanding (p0032). This sits at the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for ordered services only), so no redline is required. We note separately that Contractor may change rates on 30 days' notice under p0014 with no uplift cap — a pricing point outside this rule and addressed, if at all, under the pricing rule rather than here.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: 2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.
rationale: There is no auto-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement (no instance of "renew"). The term runs from the effective date until terminated, and § 6(a) lets either party terminate for any or no reason on fifteen (15) days' notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding, with fees priced per Statement of Work. That means there is no automatic renewal term, no non-renewal notice window to compute, and no renewal price uplift — an exit right shorter than the preferred 30 days, so the structure meets (and on exit is better than) our preferred position. Noted but not flagged here: § 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice without a cap; that is a pricing-escalation point addressed under the fees rule rather than the renewal rule, and our 15-day walk-away right limits the exposure.

verification.notes: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the redline is unchanged with no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding. Deterministic check (notice window = 15 days ≤ 60) corroborates compliance; treating the structure as compliant rather than 'missing' is correct because the absence of an auto-renewal mechanic raises no negotiation issue for us. Upon receipt of final payment Contractor shall provide to Company, and will assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

There is no obligation on Contractor to provide transition assistance, to return Company data, Works or Confidential Information in a usable format within a fixed period, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards; searches for "return", "transition" and "delete" return nothing, and the confidentiality clause (p0038-p0040) contains no return-of-materials mechanic. Inserted the preferred language as a new Section 6(d): up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return within thirty days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter; 90 days of assistance is an acceptable fallback.

quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
rationale: Contrary to the planner's hint that insurance was absent, § 7 para 14 (p0048) contains an insurance covenant binding the Contractor. It delivers several preferred elements: workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, professional E&O of USD 1,000,000 (which meets the fallback E&O limb), and certificates of insurance on Company request with notice of material change. However, it contains no cyber/privacy liability coverage at any level. That is material here rather than cosmetic: § 8 (p0038) defines Confidential Information as including Company data and records obtained by Contractor, and § 1(c) (p0007) contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems. The fallback position requires E&O USD 1M *and* cyber USD 2M; with cyber missing entirely, the clause fails the fallback on a material term for a vendor that processes our data, approaching the walk-away concern. The redline therefore makes the smallest possible edit — inserting a cyber/privacy limb at the preferred USD 5,000,000 where Contractor processes Company data — and leaves the remainder of the bargain untouched. Two sub-elements short of preferred are noted but not flagged: the CGL limb states a per-occurrence figure without the USD 2,000,000 aggregate, and E&O sits at USD 1,000,000 rather than the preferred USD 2,000,000 (expressly acceptable at fallback). The permitted reliance on "self-insurance" is likewise a minor point only. Given the engagement is a task-by-task consulting arrangement performed largely at Contractor's own facility, the comment offers USD 2,000,000 cyber as a sensible fallback landing zone.

quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: Substance is at or above the fallback, but the affiliates element is carried only by inference, so I am flagging this for reviewer sign-off rather than asserting clean compliance, and attaching an optional clarifying redline. What the clause already achieves: § 4(c) (p0021) grants a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual licence of Contractor's Information, with no revocation or at-will termination mechanic anywhere (§ 6 termination at p0032-p0033 contains no licence clawback), and a broad use scope ("in connection with Company's business operations") rather than internal use only. Affiliates and contractors are never named in the agreement - the word "Affiliate" appears nowhere - so coverage depends on reading the unconditional "right to grant a sublicense" as a self-executing path to extend the licence to affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf. That reading defeats the walk-away trigger (excluded with no path to add them) and is at least as favourable as the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice), but it is a phrasing variant rather than express words, which is why this is needs_review. The proposed edit is a drafting clarification of the existing bargain, not a scope grab: it names our Affiliates and contractors as licensees, adds the express "irrevocable" label to match the existing perpetuity, and confirms transfer to a successor in a merger or acquisition (today left to the mutual § 10 nonassignability clause at p0042, where consent "will not be unreasonably withheld"). The grant runs in our favour (Company = Clear Capital; Contractor = RadialSpark), so this is not a deviation to be pressed hard - if RadialSpark resists, the fallback of adding affiliates on written notice, or leaving § 4(c) as drafted, remains acceptable.

The promised proposal was not produced. By the playbook's own classification semantics this clause should be recorded as compliant at/near the preferred position, not escalated: § 4(c) grants a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual licence with an unconditional sublicence right, there is no at-will revocation (deterministic check confirms), and use scope is business-wide rather than internal-use-only. The absence of the express word 'Affiliate' is a minor sub-element that the rule says should be noted in the rationale, not flagged. The grant runs in our favour (Company = Clear Capital is the licensee), and the unrestricted sublicence right already provides the 'path to add' affiliates and contractors that defeats the walk-away trigger and satisfies the fallback; re-opening it risks the counterparty narrowing a clause that currently benefits us. Assignment/successor transfer is already addressed by § 10 with a reasonableness qualifier on consent; the rationale concedes this, so the successor-transfer element does not independently justify escalation.
